source_text: II. Public Comment. Ron Voigt stated he was recently contacted by a vending company that owns and operates vending machines out of Tokyo, Japan. They sell snacks and drinks. They had found out from a competitor that they did not need to collect sales tax on what they sell. They had been collecting sales tax. They came to the Department and the Department agreed that they should not have been collecting sales tax. The Department then advised them not to request a refund because they will get audited. Mr. Voigt stated the better response would have been to show the taxpayer how they arrived at their position by telling the taxpayer they shouldn’t be collecting sales tax. Was there any recent court positions? The Department needs to take the time to meet with the taxpayer and explain why they say what they say, mostly when it's done in person. Mr. Voigt asked the Department to do some type of tax note to educate the public. The Japanese snacks have become very popular with American kids. Thank you very much. Director Hughes administered an oath to all parties testifying.

source_text: 25. PUBLIC COMMENT (3:34:56) -Mayor Bagwell entertained final public comments. Mr. French noted that he had not seen “expandability” in the presentations. He also commended Ms. Sullivan and her team for the Listening Tours. Ms. Nietz expressed disappointment that the consultants had not come to this meeting in person. She also believed that there were mathematical errors in the presentations and did not believe that housing availability issue. She was disappointed that the growth concerns were placed at the bottom of the slides and did not believe that “there is no traffic problem in Carson City.” Barbara Henry stated that Emerson Drive had no speed limit signs and now they have two; however, many out-of-county drivers were using it as a shortcut and speeding in their neighborhood. She believed that 2026 was too late to remedy the situation as she had already lost a dog to speeders. Ms. Henry recommended a looping road around the City, similar to Las Vegas.

He stated that updates were indicated in bold, and staff was available to answer any questions. He highlighted that Planning Manager Lyon did a recent BC Insider regarding the City’s historic preservation program, available resources and grant. He also discussed Lisa LaPlante, the City’s Communications Manager, efforts on promoting historic preservation on various media outlets. In response to Chairman Davenport, Planning Manager Lyon stated she can add a link to the BC Insider on the City’s Historic Preservation Webpage.

Presentation of the Boulder City Museum and Historical Association’s Annual Report A staff report was submitted by City Manager Ned Thomas and included in the February 10, 2026 City Council agenda packet. John Calvert, Board Chairman of the Boulder City Museum and Historical Association (BCMHA), presented a PowerPoint summarizing museum programs and provided a financial update, noting the $950,000 mortgage on the Boulder Dam Hotel had been paid off. He expressed gratitude for the Dan Bunch Estate’s donation of approximately $310,000 and numerous Desert Sands pottery pieces. He reported that, through these funds and prudent management, BCMHA’s emergency savings reached industry standards, supporting long­term stability. He said funds had been allocated to the Avenue C House Preservation Project; creation of a Research Room and Digitizing Room; a new Desert Sands Pottery Exhibit; and improvements to three permanent exhibits.He said the organization’s major focus this year was preparing for the next century of historical preservation. source_text: 4. Presentation by Michelle Johnston, Director of Behavioral Health for U.S. VETS on veteran services and the Annual Stand Down event. (For Discussion Only) Director of Behavioral Health for U.S. VETS, Michelle Johnston, emphasized her strong commitment to supporting the veteran community. She stated that respect, kindness, and understanding are essential in helping veterans reach their full potential. She also highlighted that U.S. VETS is dedicated to ending homelessness within the community. She outlined the wide range of resources offered through the U.S. VETS program, including permanent and affordable housing, lifetime rental subsidies, temporary financial assistance, eviction-prevention support, life-skills training, on-site job fairs, legal services, comprehensive support services, counseling, outreach, and additional veteran-focused programs. Ms. Johnston also announced that the Annual Veteran Stand Down event will take place next week on Wednesday, March 4th, from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. She concluded by reaffirming U.S. VETS’ dedication to serving veterans and strengthening the community. ACTION: DISCUSSED

(Ward 1 – Barron) (For Discussion Only) Redevelopment Specialist, Scott Carter, discussed the EPA Brownfield Assessment Grant, which maintains safe and sustainable redevelopment standards. He added that this grant will encourage property owners to assess and identify potential environmental hazards, which ultimately enhance property values. Mayor Goynes-Brown inquired whether abandon buildings qualify for the program. Redevelopment Specialist, Scott Carter, noted that there has to be some sort of activity in the building in order to qualify for the program. Councilwoman Garcia-Anderson inquired whether the assessment grant is available for any business located in the RDA. Presentation by Cynthia Sneed regarding the Finance Department annual update to the City Council A staff report was submitted by Finance Director Cynthia Sneed and included in the January 13, 2026 City Council agenda packet. Finance Director Sneed provided an overview of the PowerPoint included in the agenda packet. Council member Ashurst said she appreciated that the Finance team meets regularly with department heads to determine the best use of funds and that it followed best practices. In response to Council member Ashurst, Finance Director Sneed said 75 percent of households received a physical bill in the mail and 25 percent chose the electronic option which was the most cost effective. In response to Council member Jorgensen, Finance Department Sneed said residents could enroll for online billing by calling the Utility Office or by visiting the City’s website.. Council member Jorgensen thanked the Finance Department for listening and responding to Council. She said she appreciated the City achieving a balanced budget. BILLS

CITY MANAGER MIKE JANSSEN shared that staff was coordinating with the appropriate state agency and that meetings were being scheduled to address gaps in communication. COUNCILWOMAN SUMMERS- ARMSTRONG noted concerns regarding multiple types of state-licensed group homes, including childcare facilities, drug rehabilitation homes, and elderly group homes, and emphasized the need Tor earlier coordination between the State and the City to prevent conflicts with local code requirements. MAYOR BERKLEY agreed and noted that the issue may require further discussion and potentially a legislative solution if necessary COUNCIL MEMBER RECOGNITION

plain_english_explanation: I. Review Current Information Signs and Provide Accurate Updates. KEC will review the text and images of 41 existing information signs, consisting of 30 outdoor signs and 11 indoor signs. Outdated, incorrect, or misleading information discovered during this review will be corrected, and missing information will be added. In addition, this review will ensure all dates are accurate based on the Development Timeline found in Chapter 4 of the report. Dates for any work completed after the current signs were created will be added. Note: There are four signs currently at the park for features that are no longer extant (i.e., the Turkey House, Tennis Courts, Cook House, and Gun House). These were not included in the Kautz Report and may require additional research. Historic Preservation Commission July 22, 2026 - Page 29 -- 29 of 41 -- 2

title: 18. Public hearing on local improvement district for Special Improvement District No. 1485 - Alta Drive (Landscape Maintenance - FY 2027) - Ward 1 (Knudsen)
